page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing the AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 3111.48 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2019.0, both placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 16728.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 47465.6. Cryptographic capabilities are notable, as evidenced by a strong Passmark CPU encryption test score of 38961.53, supported by hardware-accelerated instruction sets including AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. Memory performance is robust, with a Passmark memory score of 2882.22 and cached read-only memory bandwidth reaching 2464.13 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.c8ae.8xlarge is its compute-centric resource allocation. With only 2.0 GB of RAM per core and no local NVMe storage, it is less suitable for memory-intensive databases or workloads requiring high-speed local scratch space. However, its dedicated CPU allocation, strong single-core execution, and 20 Gbps network baseline make it highly cost-efficient for compute-bound tasks. Recommended workloads include web serving, software compilation, image and text processing, and multi-threaded decompression tasks.
